original_question: Which metal is found in the active site of the enzyme that is deficient in xanthinuria?

final_qi.question: Which metal is found in the active site of the enzyme that is deficient in xanthinuria?
final_qi.long_answer: Xanthinuria results from a deficiency of xanthine oxidase (xanthine dehydrogenase/oxidoreductase). The catalytic center of this enzyme contains a molybdenum-pterin cofactor; molybdenum is the essential metal that participates directly in the oxidation of xanthine to uric acid. Hence, molybdenum is the metal present in the active site of the enzyme lacking in xanthinuria.

0.question: Which enzyme is deficient in xanthinuria?

final_answer.long_answer: Hereditary xanthinuria results from deficiency of xanthine oxidase (xanthine dehydrogenase), whose catalytic center contains a molybdenum cofactor. The molybdenum atom is essential for the enzyme’s redox chemistry that converts xanthine to uric acid; absence or malfunction of this molybdenum-dependent enzyme leads to the accumulation of xanthine seen in xanthinuria.
